overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Cup of Blessing and a New Chapter
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 51a–51b
overview.hebrewSource: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּכוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf finishes the chapter on blessings over food. It rules on one who forgot to bless before eating, wanders into the folk-medicine of asparagus (an early-morning wine or beer drink) and the warnings of angels, and then lays out the ten requirements of the cup of blessing used for Grace after Meals. The story of Ulla refusing to send the cup to Yalta ends in four hundred smashed barrels. A new chapter then opens: the mishna lists every dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel concerning a meal, beginning with which comes first in kiddush, the blessing over the day or over the wine.

slides.title: 🧄 Ate Without a Blessing: Can He Still Bless?
slides.subtitle: Rav Ḥisda's answer, Ravina's extension, and where the Gemara draws the line

nodes.content: ❓ They asked Rav Ḥisda: one who ate and drank and did not recite a blessing, does he go back and recite it now?
🧄 Rav Ḥisda: Should one who ate garlic and now smells go eat another garlic so he smells more? He must bless before continuing to eat.
➕ Ravina: therefore even if he finished his meal, he goes back and blesses. Proof: one who immersed recites עַל הַטְּבִילָה only after emerging.

columns.label: Immersion
columns.content: Before immersing the man was unfit to bless (he was impure), so blessing afterward is the only option.

columns.label: Eating
columns.content: Before eating he was fit to bless. Since he was excluded once the meal ended, he stays excluded: הוֹאִיל וְאִידְּחִי — אִידְּחִי.

nodes.content: ✅ Result: bless before continuing a meal, but once it is over the opportunity is lost.

callout.label: Also on the daf:
callout.text: Why must one spit out food in his mouth rather than push it aside to bless? Rabbi Yoḥanan (via Rav Yitzḥak Kaskesa'a): יִמָּלֵא פִי תְּהִלָּתֶךָ, 'My mouth will be filled with Your praise' (Psalms 71:8), so praise is said with the whole mouth.

slides.title: 🌿 Asparagus: Every Contradiction Is Wine vs. Beer
slides.subtitle: The Sages' six rules for the morning drink, and how the Gemara reconciles clashing baraitot
rows: Good for L-E-T (heart, eyes, spleen) or R-M-T (head, intestines, hemorrhoids)?
Good for L-E-T, harmful for R-M-T
Good for R-M-T, harmful for L-E-T
Yes, when made with old wine (proof: the konam vow in Nedarim)
Not the subject of that baraita
Only its own kind (e.g. dates after date beer)
If he spits, he is harmed
If he does not spit, he is harmed
Its saliva may be expelled even before the king, since not spitting is dangerous

callout.label: The six rules:
callout.text: Drink it undiluted and from a full cup; receive it in the right hand and drink with the left; do not converse after it and do not pause during it; return the cup only to the one who handed it to you; spit after it; and supplement it only with its own kind.

slides.title: 🏆 Ten Things Said About the Cup of Blessing
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Zeira in the name of Rabbi Abbahu, and how much of the list Rabbi Yoḥanan kept

boxes.title: The full list of ten
items: Undiluted wine, and a full cup
Take it in both hands, then place it in the right
Lift it a handbreadth from the ground; fix your eyes on it
Some say: also send it as a gift to one's household

boxes.title: Rabbi Yoḥanan: only four
items: Full — and whoever blesses over a full cup receives 'a boundless inheritance' (Deut. 33:23); Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina: he inherits both worlds

boxes.title: How the Sages did it
items: Adorning: Rav Yehuda surrounded the cup with students; Rav Ḥisda with other cups
Wrapping: Rav Pappa wrapped himself in his cloak; Rav Asi spread a cloth on his head
Both hands: 'Lift your hands in holiness and bless the Lord' (Psalms 134:2)
Lift a handbreadth: 'I will lift the cup of salvation' (Psalms 116:13)
Left hand assisting the right? Unresolved by the early Sages, so Rav Ashi rules stringently

callout.label: Rav Asi adds:
callout.text: One does not speak over the cup of blessing, and one does not bless over a 'cup of punishment' — Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: a second cup. A baraita agrees: one who drinks in pairs should not bless, for 'Prepare to meet your God, O Israel' (Amos 4:12), and such a person is not prepared.

slides.title: 🍇 Ulla, Rav Naḥman, and Yalta's Four Hundred Barrels
slides.subtitle: Who must receive the cup of blessing for the household to be blessed?

lines.speaker: Rav Naḥman
lines.text: Master, please send the cup of blessing to Yalta.

lines.speaker: Ulla
lines.text: No need. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: the fruit of a woman's body is blessed only through the fruit of a man's body, as it says וּבֵרַךְ פְּרִי בִטְנְךָ — 'the fruit of your body' (Deut. 7:13), not 'her body'. Rabbi Natan taught the same in a baraita.

lines.speaker: Yalta
lines.text: (Hearing this, she rose in a rage, went into the wine store, and broke four hundred barrels of wine.)

lines.speaker: Rav Naḥman
lines.text: Let the Master send her another cup.

lines.speaker: Ulla
lines.text: (Sending a different cup:) All the wine of this barrel is wine of blessing.

lines.speaker: Yalta
lines.text: From itinerant peddlers come empty words, and from rags come lice.

callout.label: Why the cup mattered:
callout.text: The tenth item on the list — sending the cup to one's household — is 'so that his wife will be blessed'. Ulla held that giving it to the husband already accomplishes that.

slides.title: ⚖️ New Chapter: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel at the Meal
slides.subtitle: The mishna's list of disputes, beginning with kiddush
rows: Bless the day, then the wine — the day brings the wine, and the day was sanctified before the wine arrived
Bless the wine, then the day — the wine enables kiddush; and the frequent (תָּדִיר) precedes the infrequent
Wash hands, then mix the cup
Mix the cup, then wash hands
Sweep the house, then wash (final waters)
Return to where he ate and bless
Bless where he remembered (both: until the food is digested)

callout.label: 'The halakha follows Beit Hillel':
callout.text: The Gemara asks why the Tosefta needs to say so, since a Divine Voice already proclaimed it. Either the Tosefta predates the Divine Voice, or it was taught afterward — and the answer continues on the next daf. The mishna also rules that one answers amen after a Jew's blessing but after a Samaritan's only once the whole blessing is heard.

summary.principle: A blessing must be said before one continues eating, and the cup over which Grace is recited deserves rinsing, washing, undiluted wine, and fullness — a full cup brings a boundless inheritance.

flowSteps.content: 🧄 Forgot to bless: Rav Ḥisda — bless before continuing (garlic); once the meal ended, the chance is gone
🌿 Asparagus baraitot contradict → wine vs. beer; angels warn: cloak, washing, asparagus cup, women returning from a burial
🏆 Ten things of the cup of blessing; Rabbi Yoḥanan keeps four: rinse, wash, undiluted, full

columns.content: 🍇 Ulla: the wife is blessed through her husband's cup — Yalta breaks 400 barrels
🍷 Rav Asi: no talking over the cup; no blessing over a second cup (pairs)

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: New chapter — Beit Hillel: wine before the day, because the frequent precedes the infrequent; halakha follows Beit Hillel

quiz.q: What did Rav Ḥisda mean by asking whether one who ate garlic should eat another garlic?
o: That one who forgot a blessing should skip the rest of the meal
That one who forgot to bless must bless before continuing to eat, rather than adding to the lapse
That garlic does not require any blessing
That blessings are never recited after eating has begun
quiz.e: Rav Ḥisda's analogy teaches that one should not compound the failure to bless by continuing to eat without a blessing; he must recite it before going on.

quiz.q: Why does the Gemara reject Ravina's proof from the blessing over immersion?
o: Because immersion has no blessing at all
Because the immersion blessing is recited before immersing
Because before immersing the person was unfit to bless, whereas before eating he was fit and is now excluded
Because eating is a rabbinic obligation and immersion a Torah obligation
quiz.e: In the case of immersion the man could not bless earlier because he was impure; one who could have blessed before eating and did not has been excluded, and 'since he was excluded, he is excluded'.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara resolve the baraitot that say asparagus is both good and harmful for the intestines, and that spitting after it both does and does not cause harm?
o: One baraita refers to asparagus made of wine, the other to asparagus made of beer
One refers to morning, the other to evening
One refers to the sick, the other to the healthy
The baraitot are simply in dispute
quiz.e: Every contradiction on the daf about asparagus is resolved the same way: one baraita speaks of wine-based asparagus and the other of beer-based.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, which of the ten things said about the cup of blessing do 'we' actually have?
o: Adorning, wrapping, lifting, and gazing
Rinsing, washing, undiluted wine, and a full cup
Both hands, right hand, a handbreadth, and a gift to the household
All ten
quiz.e: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: we have only four — rinsing (inside), washing (outside), undiluted, and full.

quiz.q: Why did Ulla refuse to send the cup of blessing to Yalta?
o: Because women may not drink from the cup of blessing
Because the cup had already been drunk
Because Rabbi Yoḥanan taught that a woman's offspring are blessed through the man, from 'He will bless the fruit of your body'
Because the cup was a second cup, a cup of punishment
quiz.e: Ulla cited Rabbi Yoḥanan: the verse says 'the fruit of your [masculine] body', so giving the cup to Rav Naḥman suffices for his wife to be blessed. Yalta responded by breaking four hundred barrels of wine.
